stem: A point \(A(x, y)\) lies in the region bounded by the \(y\)-axis, \(2y + x = 6\) and \(5x - 6y = 30\). The probability that \(y < 1\) is:
solution: The three boundary lines meet pairwise at \((0, 3)\), \((0, -5)\) and \((6, 0)\), so the region is the triangle with those vertices. Its area is \(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6 = 24\). The line \(y = 1\) cuts it at \((0, 1)\) and at \((4, 1)\) on \(2y + x = 6\), so the part with \(y > 1\) is the triangle \((0,1), (0,3), (4,1)\) of area \(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4 = 4\). Hence \(P(y < 1) = \dfrac{24 - 4}{24} = \dfrac{5}{6}\). That value is neither \(\tfrac{1}{4}\) nor \(\tfrac{5}{9}\), and option (c) states no value at all, so the correct choice is None of these. Matches option D.
reviewNote: FLAWED - the correct probability is 5/6, which is not printed. Options A (1/4) and B (5/9) are both wrong; option C is not a value at all but a restatement of the method; option D is None of these. Strictly, D is the only defensible letter, since 5/6 is none of A, B or C. Key C is retained for OMR parity with the teacher's issued key AND because the paper's own solution endorses the area-ratio wording, but a student who correctly computes 5/6 will reasonably bubble D and would be marked wrong. Recommend this question be dropped from scoring rather than graded. Subtopic note: this is geometric (area-based) probability; the supplied Probability subtopic list has no geometric-probability bucket, so 'Probability via Counting' is the nearest fit (favourable measure over total measure) - please re-file if a better subtopic exists.

stem: An urn contains 6 white and 9 black balls. Two successive draws of 4 balls are made without replacement. The probability that the first draw gives all white balls and the second all black is:
solution: The first draw takes 4 balls from 15, so \(P_1 = \dfrac{\binom{6}{4}}{\binom{15}{4}} = \dfrac{15}{1365} = \dfrac{1}{91}\). Four white balls having gone, the urn holds 2 white and 9 black, so the second draw of 4 from 11 gives \(P_2 = \dfrac{\binom{9}{4}}{\binom{11}{4}} = \dfrac{126}{330} = \dfrac{21}{55}\). By the multiplication rule the required probability is \(P_1 P_2 = \dfrac{1}{91} \times \dfrac{21}{55} = \dfrac{21}{5005} = \dfrac{3}{715}\). Matches option B.
subtopic: Conditional Probability, Total Probability, and Bayes' Theorem
reviewNote: FLAWED - the correct answer 3/715 is not printed. This is the standard NCERT result. Option B was almost certainly INTENDED to be 3/715 (correct numerator) and is misprinted as 3/256 - re-read at 12x zoom, the denominator is unambiguously 256. Options A (5/715) and C (1/715) are exactly equidistant from the true value, so there is no nearest option. Key A is retained only because it is the issued key. The paper's own worked solution reaches the correct product and then fudges it: it writes '= 1/715 x 4.2 ... (approx 5/715 after simplification)', which is arithmetically wrong twice over (4.2/715 = 0.00587, 5/715 = 0.00699, true value 3/715 = 0.00420). Recommend dropping from scoring, or accepting B if the teacher confirms the 256 is a typo for 715.

stem: Two sets of data have 10 and 20 observations with means 10 and 20 and variances 4 and 9 respectively. The combined variance is:
solution: The combined mean is \(\bar{x} = \dfrac{10(10) + 20(20)}{30} = \dfrac{500}{30} = \dfrac{50}{3}\). The group means deviate from it by \(d_1 = 10 - \tfrac{50}{3} = -\tfrac{20}{3}\) and \(d_2 = 20 - \tfrac{50}{3} = \tfrac{10}{3}\). Then \(\sigma^2 = \dfrac{n_1(\sigma_1^2 + d_1^2) + n_2(\sigma_2^2 + d_2^2)}{n_1 + n_2} = \dfrac{10\left(4 + \tfrac{400}{9}\right) + 20\left(9 + \tfrac{100}{9}\right)}{30} = \dfrac{266}{9} = 29.56\) to two decimal places. Matches option B.
subtopic: Dispersion — Standard Deviation, Variance, Mean Deviation
reviewNote: FLAWED - no correct option. The combined variance is exactly 266/9 = 29.5556, derived two independent ways (deviation-from-combined-mean form and the n1n2(m1-m2)^2 form). The printed options are 24.33, 29.33, 30.00, 25.50, re-read at 9x zoom. Key B (29.33) is 0.22 away and C (30.00) is 0.44 away, so B is the nearest but is not correct. The paper's own solution writes the correct expression and then mis-divides: its own numerator 886 over 30 is 29.53, not the 29.33 it records - so option B looks like a typo for 29.53, which is itself a rounding of the true 29.56.
